newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1996 GDP growth seen slowing to 6.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1996 GDP growth seen slowing to 6.7 pct.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday he expected the Thai gross domestic product to slow to 6.7 percent growth in 1996 from 8.6 percent in 1995.

Rerngchai told reporters after he briefed the Thai cabinet on the economy that the Thai current account deficit, hurt by zero-growth exports, would likely widen marginally to 8.2 percent of GDP this year from 8.1 percent in 1995.
He said, however, that inflation would likely be steady at its 1995 level of 5.8 percent.
The governor said he proposed to the new government of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to cut major spending on aircraft and weapons.

"Thailand spends about 30-40 billion baht ($1.2-1.6 billion) a year on commercial and military aircraft and on arms and weapons. It would greatly help the economy if we can cut back on these items," he said.

Rerngchai confirmed an earlier central bank projection that Thai exports would post zero growth this year, their worst performance since 1983. He said sales of fishery products would fall about 13 percent this year partly because of Thai-Burmese fishing disputes.

The governor expressed optimism that the Thai industrial slowdown in the past three to four months should have bottomed out and the sector should see recovery in the months ahead under proper economic management.
He said economic problems this year could partly be attributed to Thailand's active foreign borrowing, which amounted to a combined $44 billion in the past three to four years.
The governor said the influx of foreign funds had encouraged speculation in the property sector and wasteful consumer spending.
